chapter_theme: Songs at Kundrakudi (குன்றக்குடி), also named Mayuragiri, the peacock hill: the poet asks to leave the sorrow of women, the net of lovemaking that wastes his knowing mind, and the love-sickness of moon, cuckoo and Kama's arrows; the praise names Murugan as teacher of Siva and Agastya, Rama's and Krishna's nephew, and the vel at which Death's servants tremble.
structure_note: Seven songs. 623, 625, 627 are courtesan confessions with a single plea; 624 is a vast song of breasts and battle drums; 626 an abusive catalogue of courtesans; 628 and 629 use the love-sickness motifs (moon, cuckoo, flute, gossip). Vayalur is named with Kundrakudi in 624 and 625.

623.reading: The poet asks when he will leave the sorrow of women whose moon faces, nectar speech, gait with anklets and bells, and two poison eyes that whirl the heart, draw him. The praise names Rama, the cloud-dark one who rejoiced when Kumbhakarna's younger brother came and bowed, and won Lanka's golden city, Murugan as the guru who stood and spoke the mantra while Siva, axe in hand, bowed to him, at the rich town of Kundram.
623.nuance: மழு உகந்த செங்கை அரன் உகந்து இறைஞ்ச மநு இயம்பி நின்ற குருநாதா: the Siva-teaching story with Siva bowing and the teaching called மநு, the mantra. எழுது கும்பகன் பின் இளைய தம்பி is Vibhishana coming over to Rama.

624.reading: At great length the poet describes women's breasts with elephant tusks, golden pots and pearl-bearing rivers, their dark fragrant hair, their voices of peacock and cuckoo, their eyes like Death's fortress, nail marks, slipping bangles and bitten lips, and says that in the net of lovemaking his knowing mind was wasted; he asks whether Murugan of Vayalur and lord of Kundrakudi will not grant that he think of his feet so that birth ends. The praise is a long run of drum syllables and a battlefield of vultures, ghouls and jackals, where Murugan broke the demons' armies and gave the gods protection.
624.nuance: வருமறலி அரணமொடு முடுகு சமர் விழியிணைகள: the eyes are Death's fortress pressing into battle, a link the poet often draws between lust and Death. என தறிவுடைய கலைபடுதல் is the waste of knowledge in lust; the cure is உந்திப் பிறப்பற நினைந்திட உன் அடி. The image-chains in the first half are hard to divide in places.

625.reading: The poet asks whether he will give up the pleasure of women whose breasts are like great pots, their lips, their dark hair, their sounds like bees, cuckoos, peacocks and quails, the nail marks and the swoon of union on the shoulder. The praise names Murugan whose vel made the demons break, the seven seas cry out and Yama's servants tremble asking 'what shall we do?', who rides the storm-wind peacock, dwells at Vayalur and Kundram where Ambikapati and Ganapati live, and is worshipped by Indra, Hari, Brahma, sun and moon.
625.nuance: எமபடரும் என் செய்வோம் என நடுநடுநடுங்க: Death's servants, whom the confessions fear, are themselves made to tremble by the vel, the answer to the death-hour plea told as praise.

626.reading: The poet pours out abuse of courtesans: frauds of pretended love and display, foul-mouthed, keeping company with base men for their money, swearing without shame 'you are me and I am you', liars who stand and show off, who torment whoever they cling to, painted beauties who flash their skin and cry 'oho, come, come', and asks whether a relationship with them is fit even if they come near. The praise names Krishna who silently drank Putana's life and defeated the demons Kamsa sent, Murugan who destroyed Sura's host, and Mayura hill, Kundrakudi, ringed by the river Thenaru.
626.nuance: The confession is a torrent of epithets ending in -கள் (மட்டைகள், படத்திகள், பிலுக்கிகள், மினுக்கிகள், பகட்டிகள், வம்பிகள்). நீயே நானே என்றொரு சத்தியம் வாய் கூசாது ஓதும்: the oath of oneness spoken without shame is the centre of the charge. பேயானாள் is Putana.

627.reading: The poet asks whether, struck by Kama's bow through young women of sweet flattering speech, he should go the great false way that multiplies the tangle of birth, take on such a nature, shrink, let his greatness bend and his actions fail, and suffer disgraces through desire for the carp eyes of petty women. The praise names Murugan who fought Sura with all his kin until their crowns were scattered, the guru who once spoke the mantra so that the short sage gained the meaning of bliss, at Kundrakudi.
627.nuance: சிறுமை பொருந்திப் பெருமை முடங்கி: lust is told in the Kural's terms, smallness gained and greatness bent. குறுமுநி இன்பப் பொருள் பெற ... மநு உஞ்சொல் குருநாதா is Murugan as Agastya's teacher.

628.reading: A short song: the speaker asks whether he must be so bewildered, thinking ceaselessly, by the fire of the white moon, the arrows of playful Kama and the cuckoo's calling. The praise names the beautiful chest on which lie the breasts of the coral-lipped young deer of the hunters, at the peacock hill.
628.nuance: The love-sickness is told with the stock trio of moon, Kama and cuckoo (cf. 14). Nothing marks the speaker's sex or names women as the cause, and the praise ends on Valli on Murugan's chest, so this may be a lovesick girl's lament for Murugan rather than the poet's confession; the text does not settle it.

629.reading: The poet says that through the cuckoo, Kama's spear, the moon that burns daily like sunlight, the gossip of women and the flute's music, he has been deceived in the net of desire and is maddened all day, and asks not to go into the sorrow of women with arrow eyes but to be given grace to join Murugan in the high, undying state. The praise names Krishna, who climbed the mortar to steal milk and play while Yasoda did not see, Damodara and Murari, Murugan's shoulders that delight the great lady, the forest lady and the lady of the cloudy hill, at Mayuragiri ringed by the Thenaru.
629.nuance: The love-poetry machinery (குயில், மதி, வேயூது இசை, மாதர் வசை) is the poet's own state here, unlike 628: he names விழிமாதர் and asks for அழியாத மேலான பதம், release. தாமோதரன், 'rope-bellied', is the child Krishna tied to the mortar. The three ladies in the praise are not all identifiable.

links.note: Both give the courtesan's vow of oneness and show it false: the Naladiyar's woman swore never to part, like gem and thread, and turned away; 626's women swear 'you are me and I am you' without shame.
8 asks Murugan to come when Death's servants strike; 625 shows those same servants trembling at his vel, so the fear of the plea is answered in the praise.

Both are love-sickness told with the moon, Kama's arrows and the cuckoo; 14 names the speaker as a deceiver longing for women, while 628 leaves its speaker unnamed and ends on Valli at Murugan's chest.

source_issues: Song 629: corrupt characters in தாமோக முடனு஡று and உரலு஡டு (line 13), read as ஊறு and உரலூடு; also துய்ருடே (line 8), probably துயரூடே.
